title: SPINAL MUSCULAR ATROPHY WITH CONGENITAL BONE FRACTURES 2

relationships.phenotype: SPINAL MUSCULAR ATROPHY WITH CONGENITAL BONE FRACTURES 2

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 (SMABF2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ASCC1 gene (614215) on chromosome 10q22.1.

checks.claim: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 (SMABF2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ASCC1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Our patient was also found to have a homozygous frameshift variant (c.157dupG, p.Glu53Glyfs*19) in ASCC1 , thereby representing the second known case. This confirms ASCC1 involvement in a severe neuromuscular disease lying within the spinal muscular atrophy or primary muscle disease spectra.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a homozygous ASCC1 frameshift variant in a newborn with congenital bone fractures and a disease in the SMA spectrum. The name SMABF2 is OMIM nomenclature and does not appear in the paper.

checks.claim: The ASCC1 gene is located on chromosome 10q22.1.
checks.evidence_quote: This confirms ASCC1 involvement in a severe neuromuscular disease
checks.explanation: The paper does not state the gene's location. A chromosomal location added as standard nomenclature counts as supported under the rules.

paragraphs.text: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 is a severe autosomal recessive neuromuscular disorder (Oliveira et al., 2017) that begins before birth (Knierim et al., 2016). Its features include arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, respiratory distress, and congenital bone fractures (Knierim et al., 2016), with prenatal fractures of the long bones (Giuffrida et al., 2020).

checks.claim: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 is a severe neuromuscular disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: This confirms ASCC1 involvement in a severe neuromuscular disease lying within the spinal muscular atrophy or primary muscle disease spectra.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls it a severe neuromuscular disease.

checks.claim: Spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 has autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: A similar disorder was described in patients with recessive variants in two genes: TRIP4 (three families) and ASCC1 (one family)
checks.explanation: The abstract calls the variants recessive, the patient is homozygous, and a male sibling was also affected. These fit autosomal recessive inheritance, although the word 'autosomal' does not appear.

checks.evidence_quote: multiple congenital contractures (arthrogryposis multiplex congenita), respiratory distress, and congenital bone fractures

paragraphs.text: Oliveira et al. (2017) reported a patient who had generalized hypotonia and a lack of spontaneous movements as a newborn. She died within the first days of life.

paragraphs.text: Knierim et al. (2016) reported recessive loss-of-function mutations in ASCC1 and TRIP4 in patients with this disorder. Oliveira et al. (2017) also described the disorder as recessive.

checks.claim: Knierim et al. (2016) reported recessive loss-of-function mutations in ASCC1 in patients with spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on recessive loss-of-function mutations in two genes (TRIP4 and ASCC1) that encode subunits of the nuclear activating signal cointegrator 1 (ASC-1) complex.

checks.claim: Knierim et al. (2016) reported recessive loss-of-function mutations in TRIP4 in patients with spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on recessive loss-of-function mutations in two genes (TRIP4 and ASCC1) that encode subunits of the nuclear activating signal cointegrator 1 (ASC-1) complex.

checks.claim: Oliveira et al. (2017) described spinal muscular atrophy with congenital bone fractures-2 as a recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing was performed with variant filtering assuming a recessive disease model.
checks.explanation: The authors assumed a recessive model and describe recessive variants in ASCC1 and TRIP4.

paragraphs.text: Along with ASCC1 mutations, Knierim et al. (2016) found mutations in the TRIP4 gene in patients with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy and congenital bone fractures. TRIP4 and ASCC1 both encode subunits of the nuclear activating signal cointegrator-1 (ASC-1) complex.

checks.claim: Knierim et al. (2016) found ASCC1 mutations in patients with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy and congenital bone fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified homozygous and compound-heterozygous nonsense and frameshift TRIP4 and ASCC1 mutations that led to a truncation or the entire absence of the respective proteins and cosegregated with the disease phenotype.

checks.claim: Knierim et al. (2016) found TRIP4 mutations in patients with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy and congenital bone fractures.

paragraphs.text: In patients with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy and congenital bone fractures, Knierim et al. (2016) identified homozygous and compound heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in the ASCC1 and TRIP4 genes. Both genes encode subunits of the ASC-1 complex. Knierim et al. (2016) concluded that dysfunction of this transcriptional coactivator complex can cause a clinical syndrome affecting the neuromuscular system.
